data: 10/10 amazing story with absolutely amazing voice acting
Easy 10/10, would recommend to anyone looking for a great visual novel

This was the third best VN I ever played (the other two were CLANNAD and Euphoria). And, god damn, it was a mind-blowing experience! The storytelling, the atmosphere, the soundtrack, the branching paths — everything here is a piece of art crafted with love. The game gives a lot to think about — from different relationship perspectives to abstract philosophical worldviews, so that every playthrough would guarantee a unique experience for at least 15 hours, which is perfect, because it doesn't feel neither bloated nor empty. Kudos to the creators for that.

Slay the Princess is as branching as a Visual Novel can get. The way the paths split and react to your choices is just fascinating.

I love Scarlet Hollow from the same developers, and this game felt like a really refreshing change of pace. Instead of following a traditional story, it's much more about experiencing the events differently each time and just enjoying the sheer variety of all the branches.

Despite the massive number of achievements, I can proudly say that this is one of the few games where I actually unlocked all 100% of them. Completing the entire gallery in particular took a lot of time.

This game is genuinely my favorite game of all time. The fact that everything is hand drawn, and all of it is voice acted, and it’s all so BEAUTIFUL! This game also speaks to me on a deep and personal level. Thank you for making this game, it has genuinely changed my life.

A genuinely amazing game that made me feel things. The Happily Ever route is probably the one that effects me the most. I love how, despite everything, this is a love story. 

Also I fw The Razor heavy.

From what seems like a fairly standard visual novel quickly warps into a game with a ridiculous amount of branching paths that leaves you sad happy confused all manor of emotions really but ultimately whether you play a couple of hours or complete it 100% there is a great experience waiting to be had.

This game is an absolute masterpiece. I put so many hours into this game (for a visual novel at least) to fully complete it and to experience everything the game had to offer. It is definitely worth your time. Absolutely brilliant, it's only 18 bucks, you should definitely play it.

This game has a lovely narrative and empackful story telling through the multi optional answers to choose from. There isn't anything bad I got to say about the game. The devs took great care on this game to give the up most amazing game.

An absolute blast! In a very wired and twisted way, for me it feels like a bit of Disco Elysium with a bit of Inscription. The only regret I got about this game is that I didn`t played it earlier. If you see this and you are still wondering, should I buy it? YES, YOU SHOULD! and.... please don`t slay the princess xD

Slay the Princess is pretty cool. I love the craftsmanship and level of detail put into this game. The drawings are pretty cool, the characters are great with also great and fun dialogue. I don't normally play story driven "choose your path" adventure games, but the aesthetics and reality-breaking nature of the game is enough to sink 10 hours into it.
Highly Recommended :)
the only game ive went out of my way to deliberately platinum, also the only game ive bought that is already in my steam family library, genuinely might be one of my favorites ever. please play this

It's a meta story about stories in general and it's just not very interesting. Yes there are tons of branching paths and lots of work put in, but it all ends in "well this is a game and none of this makes sense and the real ending is walking way from it."

As in; Stanley Parable but without the funniness.

Has some massive ideas about morality, mortality, predeterminism, authority, and sacrifice all packed into a game that could be "finished" in just a handful of hours. A very generous game that will offer so many routes and differences between routes that 2 people won't have the same playthrough. Gorgeous hand drawn art, and phenomenal voice acting really sell this experience for me. Obsessive ideation in death and the idea of what comes after often sends me spiraling in the anxiety and dread pit for days at a time, but this games approach surprisingly didn't wield that as a weapon against me but felt more like a mutual conversation, maybe because I was ultimately in control of the narrative direction.

What I bought on a whim during the summer sale ended up being one of my favorite games of all time.

A story where every single one of your choices really does matter. The suspense and hushed secrets lying in the cracks of the narrative keeps you on the edge while you ask question after question. Even after these questions are answered the game has endless replayability, and I've finished it (and watched other people play) at least four times now. The art is absolutely gorgeous, along with the music.

To prevent spoiling anything, PLEASE get this game. You will not regret it! And I promise you that.

This game effortlessy flipflops between the most horrific nightmare fuel ever written and absolutely hilarious.

In general one of the weirdest games I've ever played (that is still serious in its core) and if you can stomach visual novels, you should definitely try this, its fairly short even when trying to see everything and cheap to boot.

Edit: the more I thought about this game, the less I liked it. Slay the Princess is a game pretending to be deep, but it's not. You don't get to learn much about the Princess, the main character, the Narrator, or the other voices. There is no solid or satisfying conclusion to the story, many questions left unanswered, and your choices doesn't change the outcome. Not really. It all leads to the same place. Same endings.

The game's meta approach to the story doesn't add much to the overall story, either.

I recommend it, but only a little bit. In the game, you repeat the story in a short loop. Based on different choices, the story develops differently. But its not like you learn anything new in any loop. The story in my opinion needs more resolution then what is given.

This is the best iteration of a visual novel that I have ever seen. Most visual novels ask you to put aside most of your preconceived notions about games to focus on the story. Slay The Princess instead drags you away from gameplay, kicking and screaming, through not only its story but its unmatched visual style and incredibly immersive music. You will play this game once, and then play it again, and then play it again, and then play it again, and every time it will be, without any exaggeration, an entirely new experience. All of that is without mentioning the themes of horror (not terror or fright) and choice that permeate through this experience, creating an entrancing, intoxicating mix of intrigue and fear that'll be enjoyable for wimps like me and seasoned horror veterans. Couldn't recommend enough- even if you think you've seen it all through a video or something, I promise you that you have not.

EDIT: They somehow made this game better. My only complaint about this game was that it ended- now it's longer! You now have no excuse not to play it.

Where do i even start, This game is absolutely beautiful, the art, the dialouge, the paths everything is so beautifully drawn written and voiced. its made me cry multiple times. please buy this game you wont regret it.

This game is the most confusing and beautiful game I have ever played. The dynamics between the Narrator and the voices is so entertaining and fits the game so well. Just in case you don't play for that long and don't believe what the game tells you at the start, then let me assure you that this game is indeed a love story.

Sometimes, you play video games that really are utilizing the medium exceptionally. Some video games would be just fine as movies, or books, or TV shows, or whatever, and while they'd be different stories in scope or whatever, they'd still be essentially the same story. Slay the Princess is not that. This *is* a video game, and the only way this story could be told is by being a video game. It's an extremely impressive feat and I can't think of many other games that play to themselves this well, and are necessarily the style of media they are. 

I wholeheartedly recommend this.

One of my top games of the past year. Beautifully written and acted narrative and a deconstruction of character archetypes and narrative tropes -- think The Stanley Parable for eldritch horror, giving way to a love story so unexpectedly that I found myself only just discovering in the moment how invested I'd become in the characters. It can be terrifying; it can be endearing. It will sometimes hurt; it will always be worthwhile in the end.

Much like love itself.

Absoloutely Amazing game.

I'm usually not one for visual novels but this one blew me away and is a solid 10/10. Its part psychological horror, part romantic comedy and part melancholic depression. I was brought to tears by the some of the endings and the whole stroy and its themes were thought provoking.

Art style is unique and has had a lot of love put into it, music is poignant and moving. VA work is fantastic with only a handful of less than perfect audio mixing in parts. barely noticable though.

Buy it, Play it, Cry and then do the other endings and ruminate on your life.

This game is simply fantastic. So many branching routes, all with their own unique themes and perspectives, and they're all so well-written. The voice acting is fantastic and so too is the music. Everything in this game harmonises; you even have the fabled "ludo-narrative resonance".
The Narrator is a fantastic and witty bastard of a character who I love to hate. I feel sorry for him, despite it all.
The Princess is, well, whatever you make of her. All paths help you to know her, and help to build the love between you and her. After all, love is built on all sorts of emotions and trust and vulnerabilities.

You should play this game. You will laugh and cry, be afraid and angry, and best of all: love every second of it.

One of the most thoroughly engaging narratives I have ever had the pleasure of experiencing, I most certainly will be revisiting this long into the future to experience every ending. This game is worth every cent and then some.

an outstanding peace of visual and narrative art, all parts of this game work so well and are on point every time, Black Tabby Games know how to craft titles that have weight and deep feeling to them, I strongly recommended this game and their sister title Scarlet Hollow, both games are outstanding, this is one of the best indie titles of this year by far, if you're not sure go try the demo first but this title is well worth your time.

i was recommended this game after my fiancé saw the trailer and i have never loved something so much. playing feels like an interactive artwork. you will always find more even after you think you're done. this game was incredible company for me while i was living abroad and then again once i was back home. with the release of the pristine edition it was everything i could ever ask for from an expansion. i would give this game every star and award i could.

10/10
I never use words like 'masterpiece' or 'work of art' when describing things I like.

But I think this one is warranted. What a beautiful synergy of engaging winding stories, an interesting and mysterious overarching story, and plentiful heartfelt, interesting, and philisophical themes about all sorts of different facets of life. And all the while, I get to experience great voice-acting, beautiful 2d art, and a calming soundtrack.

Nothing short of amazing. I really think this is a 10/10 experience.

Waiting for the Pristine Cut was worth it. Btw I am amazed how you literally cannot tell which content was original or added later unless you were actually there to compare the two versions (or unless you are a nerd and listen super carefully for VAs mics and stuff like that)

I really like the story of this game, it's interesting and a bit convoluted, however (spoiler ahead)

The final confrontation was a bit weird, I go into an argument with her, but I didn't actually disagree for the most part, but I didn't like the idea of surrendering

With that said, I actually really like the ending and it's probably my favourite part of the game, at least the one I got.

Also, the ost and the voice acting fucking slaps, it fits the game incredibly well.

This is not just an amazing game. 
It's an inspiration on game design, and how so little... ingredients, can create so much immersion and interesting stories. Great writing and game design.

The Stanley Parabol but swap out Walking Sim for Light Novel and office environment for mild fantasy theme. Good voice work, good meta, good story overall, but a little tiny bit been there done that and pretentious.
This game is absolutely amazing--the artwork, storyline, and voice acting are all executed so well! If you enjoy (or at least don't mind) horror, you will probably enjoy this game.

I was nervous when my friend told me this was a looping game… but I’d already requested it based on recommendations from friends.

But y’all…

We looped for almost SEVEN HOURS and only saw a few repeated scenes. This game is insanity supported by outstanding voices and artwork. The language is tangible and wraps you into this world where literally anything can happen. There is nothing simple about this game.

I do horror games all the time, but this had some truly disturbing scenes with just a still picture and sound effects. Hilarious scenes, too, because you want to do something and all of a sudden that option comes up and you click and … path after path after path just opens up. We never knew what to expect.

People came into the stream late and asked ‘so what’s this story about’… and it was impossible to answer.

AND THEN I check the achievements. We didn’t do this? We can do that? How do I do that? There are almost 100 achievements to get! In 7hrs I only got 32 of them! Even people who watched my stream have determined to get the game themselves, and this is rare for a regular game much less a looping visual novel.

Well done, Black Tabby Games. Well done.

I have to go get the rest of the achievements now. Get the game. Enjoy it. Bye!

I've only done 2 playthroughs of the game and both left me teary eyed, the story telling and the ideas are so complex I didn't quite understand why. I suppose I'll understand more if I play it more or talk theory with people.

This game does a very good job at making your choice(s) matter, kind of from the very beginning. And at it's core... it's a love story. Though not in the way that you would think.

I generally don't enjoy romance books or movies, but this was a joy to play. Do not spoil yourself and go in blind for the best experience. Even with my cold dead heart the game was able to get me to smile and feel warm by the end of the game.

I wish all versions of them both could know love. It broke my heart playing through this game. I cried knowing that as they both figured it out together after eating and playing games, that it wouldn't last. I tell myself that despite what I saw via the Narrator, they continued to dance under the stars, crying tears of joy as they build their life in that very moment.
"This one is soft and delicate. You molded her to love you, and she'll make for a gentle heart. Do not mourn her. She has served her purpose."

Play the game, it's not only beautiful, but the story is amazing. The voice acting is amazing. Everything is amazing.

This game is decently short while still having a Lot of substance. It really pulls you in and I was desperate to figure out what was going to happen next with each route I chose. I love the visuals and how much the princess changes based on how you start your interaction with her, and how your choices do matter within each route. I would like to complete every route and unlock each princess alteration, but for now I'm really satisfied with what I have already accomplished. I really did end up feeling for both the protagonist you play as, and the princess, and I really got hit with how much I like the relationship they foster. I'm excited to see what else the creators add to this game! ^_^ It was a wonderful game to eat up on a Saturday night.

Beautiful, clever and well written existential meta-narrative about love, loss, grief, pain, and death, accompanied by great art and music.
One of those titles you cannot say much else than just to tell everybody to experience it themselves.

This game is really something special, and I'm sure there are far better reviews who could convince you to buy it. For me, I just really believe the less you know, the better. Which is ironic in a way

It's not perfect by any means, some routes simply have less content then others (the pristine cut will amend this issue but as of now it has not released) and all paths eventually lead to the handful of choices that give you your ending. Nonetheless I am truly amazed at what this game has to offer both in it's music, writing, voice acting, and art

A word of warning if you're going for all the achievements; while the game's complex layers are interesting to explore, knocking them out can get tiring even with a skip feature, and without a guide it can be hard to tell what exactly you need to do for some of them as the game doesn't have a built in system for what choices you have and have not made yet.

i spent a month stuck lying around in a small room in a foreign country and this game was the only thing on my mind for the majority of it. the voice acting is superb (which is still an understatement). the music and the sound design are haunting. this game left such a lasting impression on me that simply rewatching a fan animation of it a few months after watching someone else play it made me feel THE ITCH. do NOT get me started on the art. this game made me feel things. i have drawn the princess in so many notebooks. the only thing i'm slightly upset about is how many achievements there are, and the fact that i simply won't have the opportunity or the energy to hunt for all of them for a while. i've also unfortunately spoiled most of the routes for myself by bingeing youtube videos (during the aforementioned month), but i assure you that slay the princess is VERY replayable (aside from... a few lines...) and enjoyable. 100/10.

EDIT: coming back to this after a few months. just finished achievement hunting. there was so much i hadn't seen. once again, get this game. it's funny, it's bold, it's getting a (FREE) major update in the next few years that'll add a ton of new stuff, the princess is hot, nichole goodnight and jonathan sims are amazing, they added a skip button?! what more could you possibly want

Beautifully written and beautifully illustrated, with many fantastic and reactive options. I'm not a big choose-your-own-adventure person but this one really stuck with me and I found it haunting in a beautiful way. 

Highly recommended for anyone who enjoys a well-told story.
I really can't do this game justice with my words. The only way to truly experience the beauty of the game is to play it for yourself.
INTERACTIVE STORY! im not sure why but i got addicted to finding the good ending, im still not sure if i got it.
This game was very easy. I slayed the princess and got the good ending in like 10 min. I feel very happy. Nothing more to see I suppose.
